answer: At every pass the toll master stacks one stone for each camel that crosses, and the pile is counted against the caravan's own manifest before the next pass opens. A violet stone carried in from another pass fails the count: at the fable of the pile the stones must match the camels that actually crossed, and a strange stone is the wrong colour. Forging the pile means bribing the toll master, stacking 400 stones and paying 7,800, while the garden mark chalked on each stone is checked nightly, so a caravan whose stones were never stacked is turned back.
